chapter: Sarah Vaughan and the Basie band
title: Collins with Art Tatum and Nat Cole; Jones on working with Sarah and Ella
summary: Collins's joke about working with Tatum and Cole, and Jones's admiration for the stamina of Sarah and Ella.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: You told me the other day to be sure and ask you about Art Tatum in Chicago.
You said, 'Write that down. Write down Art Tatum and ask me about that.'
Yeah. All right. Well, first I'll relate John Collins with Art Tatum.

John used to have a funny line to say. You know, he has a great sense of humor too. He was working with Art Tatum. He worked with Art Tatum for a year at the Three Deuces, in Chicago. And then of course Nat Cole, who was

a tremendous talent. But John would say guys would come up and ask him about different piano players. And John would say, "Man, don't ask me that. I work with Art Tatum and Nat Cole. I can't give you an opinion." And I used to -- guys would ask me about different girl singers and I said, "Well, gee whiz, I worked with Sarah Vaughan and Ella Fitzgerald. I don't know what I can tell you." You know? And I've written for and worked with a lot of them, but I mean on a day to day basis with Sarah and with Ella. You see them under so many different circumstances, on the road, some positive some negative, but to see these real professionals arise to the occasion on every trip is quite an experience. And I began to learn to admire them, you know, other than their musical ability. It's just a stamina, that drive inside. You can call it heart or whatever you want to call it.
